statement: Combined capex of the 5 largest spenders falls year on year for 2 consecutive quarters (Securities filings; by 2028-06-30)
status_at_phase_end: Not met in 2024 (toward NO): the largest spenders' capex rose year on year through the year, with combined 2024 spending projected at a record well over $200 bn and guidance for further increases in 2025.

items.summary: Wire report: the largest cloud/AI spenders said after Q3 results that capital expenditure was growing because of AI investment, would stay elevated, and would rise into the next year.
items.detail: Reuters, 'Big Tech's AI splurge worries investors about returns', 2024-10-31 (page opened via web_extract this run; only the lead paragraph was extractable: Microsoft, Meta, Amazon stepping up data-centre spending; the rest is from the search snippet of the same page).

items.summary: Financial press: capex of the four largest internet/software companies set to total well over $200 bn in 2024, a record; one spent $14.9 bn in the quarter (+50% y/y), another projected a record $75 bn for the year, and all warned spending would continue or rise in 2025.
items.detail: Bloomberg via Yahoo Finance, 'Tech Giants Are Set to Spend $200 Billion This Year Chasing AI', 2024-11-01 (verified via web_extract this run). Companies: Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Alphabet; Apple also cited.

items.summary: Market-data analysis: the four largest spenders' third-quarter capex rose sharply year on year, led by a +44% increase at one firm, as they expanded AI infrastructure.
items.detail: S&P Global Market Intelligence, 'Big Tech ramps up capex as 1st signs of AI returns emerge', November 2024 (page opened via web_extract this run, but the capex figures were only visible in the search snippet: Q3 combined $58.86 bn vs $36.95 bn a year earlier; exact publication day not shown, set to 2024-11-01 as approximation).
